Your question is saved the moment you send it, so you can close the sheet or leave the app while a slow reply cooks: on the Claude Code bridge the answer keeps coming and lands when you come back (on other servers a dropped connection is reported so you can ask again). Close the sheet and keep working on the song: when the reply lands, a gold ✦ reply badge appears in the footer, where ⚠ reports errors, and the info strip says so — tap the badge (or ✦ AI) to read it. The reply goes to the song you asked from, even if you have moved to another one.
General chat
At the top of ✦ AI, ♪ this song / ✦ Ask / ⌨ Terminal (only with the Claude Code bridge) pick which chat you are in. The general chat is not about any one song — the app, the project, music in general, messages for the terminal — so it carries no song context, cannot add annotations, and keeps its own memory on the bridge. Its log is a repo-level file (ask/general.ask.md) that the PUBLISH sheet ships with a Publish chat button (Publish all includes it). The choice is remembered on this device.
Notes from the Mac
On the Claude Code bridge each song's chat is one long-running session that remembers earlier turns, and it can carry a message to the Claude Code sessions in your terminal ("tell the terminal to push the Game Boy branch"). When the terminal writes back, the note appears in ✦ AI as a gold ✉ bubble (inbox), and the ✦ AI button shows ✉ until you open it. Notes are saved with the chat.
What Claude Code is doing now
On the Claude Code bridge, a small chip at the top right always says what the terminal's Claude Code is doing — Claude: working: … or Claude: idle — refreshed every 10 seconds; tap it for the last ten steps with their times and the latest commits. The same line sits at the top of every ✦ AI tab and in ⏳ Jobs. Without the bridge (LM Studio, no AI) none of it appears.
📷 Screenshot to Claude
On the Claude Code bridge, tap 📷 beside 🎤 Speak to send Claude a picture of the app: the AI panel steps aside (unless it's docked), the picture goes to your Mac, and a (screenshot: …) line lands in the message box — add what to look at and Send. In a browser, pick this tab when it asks what to share.
⌨ Terminal tab
Two pickers at its top choose the model the terminal gives its advisors (read-only reviews) and its builders (the agents that write code) — Opus, Sonnet, Haiku or Fable; the terminal session's own model is set at the Mac (/model). The ⌨ Terminal tab in ✦ AI sends your message straight to Claude Code in the Mac's terminal — the session that builds Night Roll — instead of the Ask tutor. Its answers come back in that tab, and the Now: line shows what it's doing; if it's busy, your message waits in its queue. 📷 works the same. If the Mac can't be reached, the message goes back into the box.
The chat is part of the song
The conversation is kept per song, whole, and it is part of the song's save: File → Publish appends everything since the last publish to <song>.ask.md beside the song (your session log — hand it to a code session later), the ● after the song title lights while chat is unsaved, and the Publish sheet lists it. Clear chat starts a fresh session on this device (it asks first if anything is unsaved; the .ask.md keeps what was saved) — on the Claude Code bridge it also tells the Mac to really start over: without this, the same long-running Claude session kept being resumed underneath a cleared-looking chat.
Session usage and Compact
On the Claude Code bridge, a small line under ✦ AI's tab strip says "N turns · ~Nk tokens · $N.NN" for the chat you're in (♪ this song or ✦ Ask — not ⌨ Terminal, which has no session of its own), refreshed after every reply and whenever you switch tabs; past 40 turns it adds "— long, Compact saves tokens". Tap Compact beside Clear chat (in-app confirm) to have the bridge summarize this chat's memory on the Mac and shrink it — the status line then reads "compacted: 172 → 1 turns · ~24k → ~3k tokens", the exact before/after the Mac measured. Compact only affects the Mac's memory of the conversation, never your saved messages or the .ask.md log. The plan usage line in ✦ AI's Recent (tap the Now: strip) shows this account's own subscription usage — this session and this week — when the bridge has seen it.
Where the model runs
File → Settings… → AI model. In this browser: pick a small model (0.4–4 GB), the first Ask downloads it once and it runs on this device's GPU, nothing leaves the device; Test checks WebGPU and whether it's downloaded. On a server: the URL of an OpenAI-compatible server — LM Studio or Ollama on this computer (http://localhost:1234) or on another machine on your network — plus an optional API key; Test lists the server's models, picks one (your last pick if the server still has it), saves, and names exactly what's wrong when it can't (server off, CORS not enabled, https page talking to an http server, no answer in 8 s). On an iPad the server must be https (Tailscale Serve). The first time you point it at a machine other than this one, it asks once before sending your notes there.
Settings save themselves
Every Settings field saves itself the moment you leave it — there is no Save button and closing never loses anything.
Asking it to act
"put an F#m chord annotation on 21.1", "mark bars 6–12 as section A", "set a tempo of 192 at bar 6" — it writes exactly that annotation (unsynced, with a ✕ in the Publish sheet like your own). "compare this to ambush" makes it read that song's notes and annotations from the repo.

MIDI
.mid / .midi / .smf / .kar / .rmi (even RIFF-wrapped) → a song — Keep local (this device only) or Create album for several at once.
NES
The .nsf, plus its .m3u if the rip has one (names the tracks) — or drop the .m3u on its own, later, to name an already-open album's tracks. Not supported: expansion-chip games (VRC6, VRC7, FDS, MMC5, Namco 163, Sunsoft 5B) — refused by name, "expansion sound chip <names> not supported". Game Boy
The .gbs, plus its .m3u, same rule as NES — and the same background capture.
Super NES
Every .spc of the album, picked together.
Genesis
.vgm / .vgz. Synth voices only — no console-audio render yet.
PlayStation
Every .minipsf plus the one .psflib, picked together. Reads Sony's standard driver (SEQ/VAB) and Square's AKAO (Final Fantasy VII/VIII/IX, Chrono Cross) — both play the console's own audio.
PlayStation 2
Every .minipsf2/.psf2 plus the one .psf2lib, picked together. Reads Sony's standard driver (SQ/HD/BD) and Square Enix's own (BGM/WD — Final Fantasy X) — both play the console's own audio. Streamed-audio rips (Ico, XIII) are refused: "this is streamed audio, not note data — Night Roll reads sequence data (notes), not pre-rendered streams".
Nintendo 64
The .miniusf files plus the one .usflib.
SoundFont
One .sf2 — its presets become track voices, not tied to a song.
New song from a recording
One .wav / .mp3 / .m4a / .aif / .flac → a new song — Untitled until Save, 4/4 at 120 bpm; ♩ Tempo from this take afterwards reads the real tempo off the clip.

SETTINGS

Every edit is kept on this device automatically — there's no switch for it. File → Save Version (⌘S) adds a dated snapshot (music + annotations); File → Versions… lists them, and the published copy. Publish is the separate, deliberate step that shares a song.

Any OpenAI-compatible server: LM Studio (turn on Enable CORS + Serve on local network) or Ollama. Test lists its models and picks one. Context = the token window the server loaded the model with (LM Studio shows it; 8192 is its default). On an iPad the server must be https (Tailscale Serve) — Help → ✦ AI.
Downloads a small model once (0.4–4 GB, kept on this device; needs WebGPU — Test checks) and runs it here. Nothing leaves the device.
Where Publish sends your songs.
1. repo
2. token
The token: Fine-grained, repository access = that repo, permission Contents: Read and write. Check confirms the pair can publish. Your annotations go to the same repo.
3. game files & instruments
When you publish an imported game, its game files and the instruments pulled from them go to this repo — separate from your songs, public so every device (and anyone you share with) hears the game's own sound. Blank: they stay on this device only.
On: meter, key and chord names stay undeclared until you work them out yourself — Ask AI still helps, nothing is volunteered. Off (Normal): they're shown as labelled estimates, never written as annotations without a tap.
For chasing a problem with Claude. Off, only real problems raise the ⚠ chip; on, the ⚠ sheet also shows what the audio engine measured, marked [debug].
On: the Pencil places, grabs and moves notes the moment it touches — no hold; fingers still hold to grab and swipe to scroll. Off: the Pencil behaves like a finger.
Off (the DAW way): selecting a note leaves the playhead where it is, so Space plays from where you were. + Note still anchors at the note you tapped.
Off (the DAW way — Logic, GarageBand, Cubasis): ● Record keeps exactly what you played, on- or off-grid. On: every key restores today's behavior, snapping starts and durations to the move grid as you play. Either way, Q Quantize straightens a take afterward, undoably.
